rulings.question: What do "Raided card" and "its top Raided card" refer to?
rulings.answer: "Raided card" refers to a card with Raid that has a face-up card under it. "Its top Raided card" refers to the very top card of a Raided card.

rulings.question: I choose a Raided card with this ability and place its top Raided card into my sideline. In this situation, do the cards under it remain on the field?
rulings.answer: Yes, they do.

rulings.question: I choose a Raided card with this ability and place its top Raided card into my sideline. In this situation, do [When Sidelined] abilities on the top Raided card and [When Played] abilities on the card remaining on the field activate?
rulings.answer: No. Neither abilities activate because the cards are not sidelined or played.

rulings.question: I choose a resting Raided card with this ability and place its top Raided card into my sideline. In this situation, does the face-up card under it remain on the field in the active state or the resting state?
rulings.answer: If the Raided card was resting, the face-up card remains on the field in the resting state. The face-up card under a Raided card retains that Raided card's active or resting state.

rulings.question: When the top Raided card is placed into the sideline, is the card remaining on the field still affected by abilities that affected the Raided card?
rulings.answer: No. Abilities that affected the Raided card lose their effect.

rulings.question: Does a character affected by "It loses all base abilities" lose abilities previously gained from abilities on itself or other cards? ・Example of an ability on itself: (CGH-1-059 Lancelot) [When Played] This character gains 1000 BP until the start of your next turn. ・Example of an ability on another card: (UE04BT/CGH-1-015 Lelouch Lamperouge) [When Played] Choose up to one character on your field. rulings.question: How do I resolve the situation when there are four cards on my front line as a result of this character being played, Raided, or moved to the front line?
rulings.answer: If the maximum number of cards that can be placed on the line changes and the number of placed cards exceeds that limit, place any one card from the line into your removal area, then reconfirm the maximum number of cards that can be placed on the line. After reconfirming, if the number of placed cards still exceeds that limit, repeat the previously described management.

rulings.question: What does the ability "Your opponent cannot choose this character with an ability on an event card unless they place one card from their hand into their sideline as an additional cost" do?
rulings.answer: When choosing a character for event card abilities like "Choose one character with 5000 or less BP on your opponent's front line and sideline it" which include the instruction to "choose" a character, this ability forces the player to place one card from their hand into their sideline as an additional cost in order to choose this character. The player may instead not pay and choose a different character. Or, if the option is allowed, they may choose zero characters. If they have no cards in their hand, this character cannot be chosen.

rulings.question: What does the "cannot be chosen by abilities" part of "cannot be chosen by your opponent's trigger abilities" mean?
rulings.answer: It means the card cannot be chosen by abilities like "Choose one character on your opponent's front line and sideline it" which include the instruction to "choose" a card.

rulings.question: When does an ability with the condition "At the end of this character's attack" activate?
rulings.answer: If a battle occurs, it will activate after the battle ends. If damage is dealt to the player, it will activate after the trigger check ends.

rulings.question: Can I check a "face-down card" placed under a card on my field to see what card it is?
rulings.answer: Yes, you can check a "face-down card" placed under a card on your field. You cannot check a "face-down card" placed under a card on your opponent's field. Place back any face-down cards you've checked in any order you wish.

rulings.question: If there are four red <Rei Ayanami> cards with 0, 1, 2, and 3 required energy respectively in my sideline, does "up to one red <Rei Ayanami> of each required energy" mean I can place those four cards face down under this character?
rulings.answer: Yes. You can place up to a maximum of four of them face down under this character in that situation.

rulings.question: While this card is resting, I place its top Raided card into my sideline for its "At the end of your attack phase" ability. In this situation, does the face-up card under it remain on the field in the active state or the resting state?
rulings.answer: If the Raided card was resting, the face-up card remains on the field in the resting state. The face-up card under a Raided card retains the Raided card's active or resting state. After that, if Raid is performed on the character again, it is switched to active.

rulings.question: When the top Raided card is placed into the sideline, is the card or newly Raided card remaining on the field still affected by abilities that affected it when previously Raided?

rulings.question: I place the top card from this Raided character into my sideline with its "At the end of your attack phase" ability. In this situation, do [When Sidelined] abilities on the top Raided card and [When Played] abilities on the card remaining on the field activate?
rulings.answer: No. Neither abilities activate because the cards are not sidelined or played. [When Played] abilities on the newly Raided card do activate.

rulings.question: What do "Raided card" and "its top Raided card" refer to?
rulings.answer: "Raided card" refers to a card with Raid that has a face-up card under it. "Its top Raided card" refers to the very top card of a Raided card.

rulings.question: I choose a Raided card with this ability and place its top Raided card into my sideline. In this situation, does the card under it remain on the field?
rulings.answer: Yes, it does.

rulings.question: I choose a Raided card with this ability and place its top Raided card into my sideline. In this situation, do [When Sidelined] abilities on the top Raided card and [When Played] abilities on the card remaining on the field activate?
rulings.answer: No. Neither abilities activate because the cards are not sidelined or played.

rulings.question: I choose a resting Raided card with this ability and place its top Raided card into my sideline. In this situation, does the face-up card under it remain on the field in the active state or the resting state?
rulings.answer: If the Raided card was resting, the base Raid card remains on the field in the resting state. The base Raid card under a Raided card retains the Raided card's active or resting state.

rulings.question: When the top Raided card is placed into the sideline, is the card remaining on the field still affected by abilities that affected it when Raided?
rulings.answer: No. Abilities that affected the Raided card lose their effect.
